messages:
nina: Quick heads-up: I rolled an RBAC update for scanner-sa to add cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter and a few CI jobs started failing with KMS PermissionDenied shortly after.

jose: which key and what command did you run?

nina: command was `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-ci --member=serviceAccount:scanner-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` targeting projects/redwood-ci/locations/global/keyRings/scan/cryptoKeys/scan-key.

ankur: saw ~6 SAST jobs fail then retry succeed. logs show `rpc error: PermissionDenied` on decrypt calls then `OK` on retry. Could be IAM propagation TTL.

lee: we should preserve all CI artifacts and snapshot GCS paths. also check Admin Activity audit log for SetIamPolicy timestamp and KMS Data Access logs for decrypt attempts.

nina: preserved artifacts under gs://redwood-ci/scan-artifacts/17691234*. uploaded executor logs to internal ticket SEC-2026-989.

infra-bot: iam-change: policy update applied by nina (run: infra-8910).

jose: interestingly some KMS Data Access entries exist but payload is minimal for two decrypt events around the time. missing principalEmail fields. that makes attribution annoying.

ankur: could be sampling/backfill on Google's side. open a GCP support case to request full payloads for the 1769123440-1769123600 window.

nina: opened case GCP-2026-1202 and attached job ids.

lee: ops mitigation: add a short-lived smoke check after any IAM rebinds: run `gcloud kms decrypt` with a test blob from a canary runner. also add checklist step to pause scanner workers during critical role flips.

jose: forensics: if audit payloads are sparse, we can reconstruct requests from executor traces and node logs. not ideal but workable.

ankur: triage note: mark the failed SAST/DAST runs as probable false positives and re-run before declaring findings. I'll start backfill runs for affected PRs.

nina: adding RBAC-change checklist PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/ops/pull/312 — includes pre-notify, preserve-audit, smoke-decrypt, and drain-scanner flags.

lee: good. also add monitoring rule: `scan.kms.decrypt_error_rate >= 5%` to trigger runbook.

infra-bot: alert-rule-create: scan.kms.decrypt_error_rate threshold=5% lookback=15m.

sec-bot: incident-candidate created: owner=nina, ticket=SEC-2026-989 severity=medium.

jose: one more ask 94 can we prefer Workload Identity for scanner runners to avoid SA token TTL issues when bindings change?

nina: agreed, long-term move to workload identity is on infra roadmap. adding note to ticket.

ankur: re-runs started, will report results.

lee: thanks all. keep SEC-2026-989 open until backfills finish and GCP responds.
